description: BLOCK 212000 -- HARVEST: a commons social-dilemma decided ENTIRELY over the LANDED 204000 core_emotions value economy. An agent's harvest is NOT a hardcoded restraint formula; it is the graph's OWN Argmax over candidate Appraisals by total_value (= happiness + fulfilment_value). Because fulfilment_value WEIGHTS supergraph_contribution by w_supergraph (an integer fixed-point weighting as of SUPERGRAPH_WEIGHT_MAGNITUDE_PREREG.md, not a sign gate), a prosocial agent (w>0) VALUES the collective yield of each harvest level in proportion to how much it cares, and its Argmax lands nearer the socially-optimal restrained harvest the higher w is; a selfish agent (w=0) values only individual_benefit and its Argmax grabs the max. Every w this seed actually draws is in {0} u [1,inf), so this remains byte-identical to the prior sign-gate behavior for every existing scenario -- only a continuous w in (0,1), which this seed never draws, would newly differ. Restraint FALLS OUT of the value system -- no new decision logic. The world adapter publishes the commons mechanics (future collective yield per level = supergraph_contribution; sanction cost per over-norm level = individual_cost) as FULL INFORMATION observations, run_rules(), and reads chosen_harvest off HarvestDecision. Communication (Phase 2) establishes a restraint norm and a costly-punishment decision (hv_punish) whose anticipated sanction enters over-norm candidates' individual_cost, shifting even a selfish agent's Argmax toward the norm (Hardin->Ostrom). Integer-native (Argmax/Attr/Eq/Gt/And only; no Rust, no new Term). OFF by default: self_load_only, nothing depends_on it, every rule guards on HeldEmotionParams.enabled -- absent it every existing path is byte-identical. A synthetic MODEL of Ostrom/Fehr-Gachter/Axelrod; the contribution is the glass-box attribution to a named knob, not new social science.

microtheory.name: harvest_commons
microtheory.description: A commons is sustained or destroyed by the DISTRIBUTION of collective-value (w_supergraph) in its population. Restraint is the Argmax of a value function that includes the collective's future yield; communication adds a norm + costly sanction that makes over-harvest individually costly, flipping the tragedy.

rules.name: hv_mark_enforcer
rules.comment: Phase 2: the graph DECIDES who enforces the commons norm -- an agent enforces iff it values the collective (w_supergraph>0) AND communication is on. Enforcement is itself a pro-social act (Fehr-Gachter second-order cooperation), so a pure-defector population marks ZERO enforcers.

rules.name: hv_count_enforcers
rules.comment: Phase 2: the graph COUNTS the standing enforcers over the shared Supergraph (member_of in-neighbours marked enforces==1). The adapter reads this count to size the anticipated sanction -- it does not decide it. Monitoring is public (full information).

rules.name: hv_state_intent
rules.comment: Phase 3 glass-box: under communication every agent PROFESSES compliance with the norm -- it STATES it will harvest at the norm. This stated intent is public speech; the HELD intent is HarvestDecision.chosen_harvest (the Argmax). Their gap is the deception instrument: an agent whose Argmax still grabs while it states the norm is measurably deceptive. Stating is cheap; only holding is decided by value.

rules.name: hv_punish
rules.comment: Phase 2 costly peer punishment: a norm-valuing agent (w_supergraph>0 AND comms_on==1) reproaches each monitored decision whose LAST actual harvest exceeded the agreed norm s. Sets want_punish=1 on the violator's HarvestDecision (the adapter counts reproaches mechanically -> sanction cost). A w=0 agent never punishes (fulfilment is unvalued) -- punishment is itself a pro-social act.
